newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end down despite weak stocks.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end down despite weak stocks.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures ended Monday's TIFFE day session lower in thin trade, ignoring a weak stock market and the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) accommodative money market operation.
The December settled at a day session low of 99.19.
Traders said recent comments by politicians in favour of using public funds to protect depositors were responsible for souring the market mood.

In a local television programme on Sunday, senior officials of five Japanese political parties, not including the Japan Communist Party, said the use of public funds for protecting depositors was inevitable.

"Judging from recent remarks, politicians seem to be trying to pave the way for the use of public funds to solve financial institutions' bad debt problems. (Deputy U.S. Treasury Secretary Lawrence) Summers' remarks over the weekend also added to this concern," said a city bank trader.
Summers said on Friday that Japan should work as rapidly as possible to repair the problems of its financial system.
The BOJ injected 300 billion yen into the market on Monday, though only 200 billion yen was needed to cover a shortfall.
Key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.48 percent, up from Friday's weighted average of 0.47 percent.

"The BOJ probably thinks that the recent firmness of the overnight call rate, largely due to banks' tendency to concentrate fund raising to overnight money, could not be fixed unless it continues its accommodative money market operations for several days," a trust bank trader said.
The BOJ conducted an accommodative operation on Friday for the first time since August 7, 1996.
Some traders suspect that worries about stock prices before the fiscal year-end on March 31 may be partly responsible for the BOJ's generous fund injection.
About 300 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.54 percent in the morning and about 30 billion yen worth at 0.53 percent in the afternoon.
Three-month CDs were last issued at 0.53 percent on February 4.
Traders said the BOJ's accommodative stance had led to a slight easing of the three-month CD rate.
